C-RELEASE-RC-CHANNEL.Summary: Publish release candidates through a dedicated npm rc dist-tag channel so default upgrades stay on latest, with an explicit opt-in upgrade path to the latest release candidate.
C-RELEASE-RC-CHANNEL.Problem: The publish workflow runs npm publish without a tag, which moves the latest dist-tag onto any published version including pre-releases. The first published release candidate would silently become the default upgrade target for every vvoc upgrade user. The existing --allow-prerelease upgrade flag resolves the highest version among all published versions instead of an explicitly managed channel, so accidental alpha or beta publications would also be picked up.

Goals.Goal: Extend publish.yml with a required release channel input that defaults to latest and passes an explicit npm dist-tag on publication, keeping the existing already-published recovery path unchanged.

Derive the release channel in release-bump from the bumped version (rc pre-release versions publish to the rc channel, everything else to latest), pass it to the publish workflow dispatch, and mark rc GitHub Releases as pre-release.
Resolve the --rc upgrade flag (and the existing --allow-prerelease flag) from the npm rc dist-tag instead of the maximum published version, so the release candidate channel is explicitly managed.
Keep the default upgrade path untouched: without opt-in flags it resolves the latest dist-tag and never offers a pre-release.
Report a clear message when the rc channel has no published candidate instead of failing or silently selecting another version.
Document the release-candidate workflow and the upgrade flags in README and keep GRACE graph and verification synchronized.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Do not add arbitrary user-named channel support; exactly one pre-release channel, rc, is managed.
Do not change the default upgrade channel, the version comparison semantics, or the post-upgrade sync and completion flow.
Do not change install pinning semantics: sync keeps pinning the exact installed version, including pre-release versions.
Do not change release gates, trusted publishing, provenance, or the exact-SHA publication policy.
Do not publish release candidates automatically from branch or tag pushes.

Constraints.Constraint: publish.yml must reject publication when the channel input is not latest or rc.
The rc channel must only ever be published through npm publish --tag rc; the latest channel must never be moved onto a pre-release version.

Channel derivation is deterministic from the bumped semver: versions containing an rc pre-release identifier publish to rc; all other versions publish to latest; an explicit channel argument, when accepted, must agree with the derivation.

Upgrade channel resolution must read the npm dist-tags endpoint for the package and degrade to a clear already-latest or no-candidate message when the rc tag is absent, never to an implicit fallback version.
Existing upgrade behavior for users without flags and the already-latest short-circuit for versions ordered above the resolved target must remain unchanged.
Workflow files, release scripts, upgrade command, README, GRACE graph, and GRACE verification stay synchronized with the implemented behavior.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: publish.yml accepts a channel input, validates it against latest and rc, and publishes with the matching npm dist-tag while the already-published recovery branch keeps skipping publication.

release-bump derives rc for bumped versions with an rc pre-release identifier and latest otherwise, dispatches publish.yml with the derived channel, and creates rc GitHub Releases with the pre-release marker.
The bump script rejects an explicit channel argument that contradicts the version-derived channel.
vvoc upgrade without flags resolves the latest dist-tag and never resolves a pre-release version.
vvoc upgrade --rc and --allow-prerelease resolve the version currently pointed to by the npm rc dist-tag, install it when newer than the current version, and report already-latest when it is not.
When the rc dist-tag is absent from the registry, the upgrade command prints a clear no release candidate message and exits successfully without installing anything.

Deterministic tests cover channel derivation from versions, dist-tag resolution and degradation, flag equivalence, unchanged default resolution, and the existing already-latest ordering including pre-release versions.

The publish workflow YAML structure, the dispatch inputs, and the release script channel plumbing are covered by repository checks, and README documents the rc release workflow and both upgrade flags.
Focused tests, repository check, build, pack check, release consistency, and GRACE validation gates pass with fresh output.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh deterministic output proves channel derivation and dispatch plumbing, dist-tag based rc resolution with absent-tag degradation, unchanged default latest resolution and already-latest ordering, workflow input validation, and synchronized documentation and GRACE state, without publishing to npm or requiring network access beyond mocked registry responses.

Assumptions.Assumption: The user explicitly approved the npm dist-tag design with exactly one managed pre-release channel named rc, the --rc flag as the canonical opt-in with --allow-prerelease kept as an equivalent alias, and an unchanged default latest channel.

Post-upgrade sync already re-pins the OpenCode plugin and TUI specifiers to the exact installed version because managed specifier matching accepts any PACKAGE_NAME@version prefix, including pre-release versions.
npm moves the latest dist-tag onto any published version when no tag is passed, including pre-releases, which is the failure mode this change closes.

Existing release gates, trusted publishing, and the exact-SHA policy remain sufficient for rc publications; an rc publication is the same CI-gated flow with a different dist-tag and a pre-release marker on the GitHub Release.
GitHub Releases created from rc bumps may be marked pre-release without affecting tag naming or the recovery flow.
